questions.template: What number is the Roman numeral III?
questions.explain: Three I's in a row: I + I + I = 3.

questions.template: What number is the Roman numeral V?
questions.hint: Hold up one hand and spread your fingers into a V!
questions.explain: V is 5 — like the shape between your thumb and fingers.

questions.template: What number is the Roman numeral X?
questions.hint: Two V's — one upside down on the other.
questions.explain: X is 10: picture two fives stacked into a cross.

questions.hint: A small I BEFORE the V takes one away.
Five… then keep counting the strokes.

questions.template: What number is XII — like on a clock face?
questions.hint: It sits at the very top of the clock.
questions.explain: X is 10 plus II — 12, the top of every proper clock.

questions.hint: I BEFORE X takes one away from ten.
Ten, then five, then one — all adding up.
Two tens… then a tricky IV.
questions.explain: XX is 20 and IV is 4 — together 24.

questions.hint: Three tens marching in a row.
X BEFORE L takes ten away from fifty.
questions.explain: L is 50; X before it takes ten away: 40.

questions.hint: X BEFORE C takes ten from one hundred.
questions.explain: C is 100; X before it makes 90.

questions.template: What number is C — as in Marcus's C push-ups?
questions.hint: C for CENTUM — a Roman century!
questions.explain: C is 100 — one glorious century of push-ups.

questions.hint: Fifty, then ten, then five — all adding.
